paper_metadata.title: Influence of heat treatment on microstructure and tensile property of a new high strength beta alloy Ti-2Al-9.2Mo-2Fe

evidence.quote: An investigation is given on the influence of heat treatment by the microstructural characteristics and tensile properties of a new high strength alloy Ti-2Al-9.2Mo-2Fe.
The Ti – 2Al – 9.2Mo – 2Fe alloy is a metastable beta titanium alloy with the β transus temperature of 815 1C.
As mentioned above, the Ti –2Al–9.2Mo–2Fe alloy is a beta alloy with the molybdenum equivalent of 15.2 and the β transus temperature of 815 1C.
The microstructural characteristic and tensile properties of the Ti–2Al–9.2Mo–2Fe alloy were investigated systematically.

attributes.location: in the beta matrix and on prior beta grain boundaries

evidence.quote: there are stubby and globular primary α phases precipitated in the β matrix, as well as discontinuous primary α phases formed on and along the prior β grain boundaries. The stubby and globular primary α phases have 2–5 μm length or diameter. However, the remaining β grains exhibit a size within 10 μm.
In case of the solution treatment at 850 °C condition, it results in equiaxed and coarse β grains with a mean size of about 50 μm due to recrystallization, as seen in Fig. 2(b).
the size scale of the ω precipitates is in the range of 10–20 nm.
The ω precipitates clearly exhibit an ellipsoidal shape with a size scale of about 30 nm seen in Fig. 3(b). It is observed that the ω precipitates have coarsened during aging at 450 °C.

Although the isothermal ω phase is less common in beta alloys when treated in the α/β-ST and aged at lower temperatures, it is detected in the alloy with the α/β-ST and aged at low temperatures (400 –450 1C).
The α phase with 1 –3 μm obtained at high aging temperatures leads to attractive combinations of strength and ductility (1200–1400 MPa of ultimate strength with 7.5 –12.5% of elon-gation).
